title: APEC economies expected to set aside differences and agree on joint statement, official says
text:
APEC economies expected to set aside differences and agree on joint statement, official says | Lianhe Zaobao 
 Singapore International China Business Opinion Lifestyle Entertainment Search Published / 17 Nov 2026 23:12 S M L XL APEC economies expected to set aside differences and agree on joint statement, official says
 AI-translated article with transliterated names. Read original Chinese article here. 
 Kuriyama said APEC members had discussed the safe and responsible use of artificial intelligence, including how it could support economic growth, employment and broader development. （AFP） A senior Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) official told Reuters on Tuesday (17 November) that the bloc’s economies were expected to set aside some differences and agree on common goals at this week’s summit in Shenzhen, despite disagreements over issues such as tariffs and supply chains. 
 Carlos Kuriyama, director of APEC’s Policy Support Unit, said the economies had a strong record of cooperation, from using artificial intelligence safely to boost economic productivity to streamlining cumbersome customs clearance procedures through digital systems. This could help keep members focused on the bigger picture in international trade. 
 Kuriyama said that despite their differences, member economies had always found ways to cooperate, from launching negotiations on a trans-Pacific trade agreement to pushing for higher environmental standards at the World Trade Organization. 
 “We have 21 economies. Despite the tensions and various concerns, everyone is keeping channels of communication open, creating opportunities to resolve problems through diplomacy.” 
 Although tensions between Beijing and Washington have recently flared again, Kuriyama said he did not believe this would derail efforts to reach a joint statement. 
 He said: “I see the US delegation working closely with other delegations to ensure that we can issue a joint statement acceptable to everyone.” 
 More broadly, he added, all 21 APEC members had expressed concern about unnecessary trade restrictions and agreed on the need to ensure that trade was not only “open” but also “fair”. 
 Kuriyama said APEC members had discussed the safe and responsible use of artificial intelligence, including how it could support economic growth, employment and broader development, but had yet to finalise the joint statement. 
 “All delegations are working day and night, and we hope to share good news with everyone later. They are working very hard to ensure that everyone can reach a consensus.”
